name: Google Workspace
description: Checks 2-Step Verification, super admin count and inactive users. Syncs user accounts.
setup_help: In Google Cloud, create a service account and a JSON key. In the Admin console go to Security > Access and data control > API controls > Domain-wide delegation, add the service account's client ID with the scope https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.directory.user.readonly. Then enter a super admin email for the service account to act as.

fields.name: admin_email
fields.label: Super admin email to impersonate
fields.help: Read-only access is used, e.g. admin@acme.in

tests.title: 2-Step Verification enforced for all active users
All active users enrolled in 2-Step Verification
Super admin count within limit
No active accounts unused for 90+ days

name: Microsoft 365 / Entra ID
description: Checks MFA policy, MFA registration and Global Administrator count. Syncs user accounts.
setup_help: In the Entra admin centre, register an app (App registrations > New registration), create a client secret, and grant these Microsoft Graph application permissions with admin consent: User.Read.All, Policy.Read.All, RoleManagement.Read.Directory and AuditLog.Read.All. MFA registration details need an Entra ID P1 licence.

tests.title: MFA required for all users (Security defaults or Conditional Access)
All member users registered for MFA
Global Administrator count within limit

name: Okta
description: Checks MFA policy and enrolment, admin count and dormant accounts. Syncs user accounts.
setup_help: In the Okta Admin Console go to Security > API > Tokens and create a token as a Read-only Administrator. Enter your Okta domain, for example acme.okta.com. For custom domains use the original okta.com domain.

fields.name: dormant_days
fields.label: Flag active users with no sign-in for (days)

tests.title: Sign-in policy requires MFA for all apps
All active users enrolled in MFA
Okta administrator count within limit
No dormant active accounts

name: Amazon Web Services
description: Checks root MFA, password policy, key rotation, CloudTrail and log retention, S3 public access, encryption, backups, GuardDuty, Security Hub and Inspector.
setup_help: Create an IAM user (or role) with the AWS managed 'SecurityAudit' read-only policy and paste its access key. Tag IAM users with 'email' so they can be matched to employees. Use the region where your production workloads run, e.g. ap-south-1 (Mumbai).

tests.title: Root account has MFA enabled
IAM password policy requires 12+ characters
Multi-region CloudTrail is logging
S3 account-level public access block is on
EBS encryption by default is on
All RDS instances are encrypted at rest
RDS automated backups retained 7+ days
GuardDuty threat detection is enabled
Security Hub is enabled with a standard (configuration baseline)
Amazon Inspector scans EC2, ECR or Lambda for vulnerabilities
AWS Backup has at least one backup plan with resources assigned
CloudWatch log groups keep logs for 180+ days
IAM access keys rotated within 90 days
Production runs in its own AWS account (AWS Organizations)

name: Microsoft Azure
description: Checks Defender for Cloud, storage encryption and public access, activity log export, subscription owners and where resources are hosted.
setup_help: Register an app in Entra ID, create a client secret, then on the subscription (Access control (IAM)) assign the app the built-in Reader and Security Reader roles. Read-only; nothing is changed.

fields.name: require_india_region
fields.label: Require all resources to be in India (yes/no)

tests.title: Microsoft Defender for Cloud enabled (Standard tier)
Storage accounts enforce HTTPS/TLS 1.2 and block public blob access
Subscription activity log exported to a workspace or storage
Subscription Owner assignments within limit
Resources hosted in Indian regions

name: Google Cloud
description: Checks project owners, public IAM grants, public buckets, user-managed service account keys and audit logging.
setup_help: Create a service account in the project, grant it the Viewer, Security Reviewer and Storage Object Viewer roles (or the narrower roles/iam.securityReviewer + roles/storage.legacyBucketReader), create a JSON key and paste it here. Read-only; nothing is changed.

tests.title: Project owner count within limit
No IAM roles granted to allUsers or allAuthenticatedUsers
Cloud Storage buckets enforce public access prevention
No user-managed service account keys
Data access audit logs enabled for all services

name: GitHub
description: Checks organisation MFA, branch protection, secret scanning, Dependabot alerts and admin count.
setup_help: Create a fine-grained personal access token (or GitHub App) owned by an organisation admin with read-only access to Administration, Metadata, Members and Secret scanning alerts for all repositories.

tests.title: Two-factor authentication required for the GitHub organisation
Default branches require pull request review
Secret scanning enabled on all repositories
Dependabot vulnerability alerts enabled on all repositories
No critical or high Dependabot alerts open past the fix deadline
Organisation admin count within limit

name: GitLab
description: Checks group 2FA, protected default branches with approvals, and owner count. Syncs members.
setup_help: Create a group access token (or a personal token of a group owner) with the read_api scope. For GitLab self-managed, enter your instance URL; it must be reachable over HTTPS from the internet.

tests.title: Two-factor authentication required for the group
Default branches protected; no direct pushes by developers
Merge requests need at least one approval
Group owner count within limit

name: Microsoft Intune
description: Checks managed devices are encrypted, compliant and checking in.
setup_help: Register an app in Entra ID, create a client secret and grant the Microsoft Graph application permission DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All with admin consent. You can reuse the Microsoft 365 app.

tests.title: Managed devices are encrypted
Managed devices meet compliance policies
Devices checked in within 30 days

name: Jamf Pro
description: Checks Macs have FileVault on, a current macOS version and recent check-ins.
setup_help: In Jamf Pro go to Settings > API roles and clients. Create a role with Read Computers and an API client using it, then generate a client secret. Enter your Jamf Pro URL, e.g. https://acme.jamfcloud.com.

tests.title: FileVault enabled on all Macs
Macs checked in within 30 days
Macs run a supported macOS version

name: Keka HR
description: Imports employees, managers, joining and exit dates for leaver checks and access reviews.
setup_help: In Keka, go to Settings > Integrations & Automation > API access (or the Keka developer portal) and create API credentials. You need the client ID, client secret and API key, and your Keka domain, e.g. acme.keka.com.

name: Darwinbox
description: Imports employees, managers, joining and exit dates for leaver checks and access reviews.
setup_help: Ask your Darwinbox admin to enable the Employee master API (Settings > Integrations > API) and share the API username and password, API key and dataset key. Enter your Darwinbox domain, e.g. acme.darwinbox.in.

name: Jira
description: Creates Jira issues for compliance tasks and risks, pulls their status back, and imports risks logged in Jira.
setup_help: Create an API token at id.atlassian.com (Security > API tokens) for a user who can create issues in the project. Enter your site, e.g. https://acme.atlassian.net, and the project key, e.g. SEC.

fields.name: min_priority
fields.label: Sync tasks with priority at least (low/medium/high)

fields.name: sync_risks
fields.label: Create a Jira issue for every new risk (yes/no)

fields.name: risk_issue_type
fields.label: Issue type for risks
fields.help: Use 'Risk' if your project has that issue type

fields.name: risk_import_jql
fields.label: Import risks from Jira matching this JQL (optional)
fields.help: For example: project = SEC AND labels = risk

name: Bitbucket Cloud
description: Checks main branches require approved pull requests and block direct pushes.
setup_help: Create a workspace access token (Workspace settings > Access tokens) with Repositories: Read, or an Atlassian API token for an account with read access (enter its email too).

tests.title: Main branches require an approval and block direct pushes

name: Snyk
description: Checks your code and dependencies are being scanned and no critical or high issue is past its fix deadline.
setup_help: In Snyk go to Settings > Service accounts and create one with the Org Viewer role (or use a personal API token). Copy the organisation ID from Settings > General. Choose your region's API host if not US.

tests.title: Code and dependencies are being scanned by Snyk
No critical or high Snyk issues open past the fix deadline

name: Tenable Vulnerability Management
description: Checks infrastructure is scanned at least monthly and critical or high findings are fixed on time.
setup_help: In Tenable Vulnerability Management (cloud.tenable.com) create API keys for a user with the Basic or Scan Operator role under Settings > My Account > API Keys.

tests.title: A vulnerability scan completed in the last 30 days
No critical or high vulnerabilities open past the fix deadline

name: CrowdStrike Falcon
description: Checks Falcon sensors on laptops and servers are reporting and no high-severity alert is left open.
setup_help: In the Falcon console go to Support and resources > API clients and keys, and create a client with read scope for Hosts and Alerts. Pick the cloud your tenant is in.

tests.title: Endpoint sensors reported within 7 days
No high or critical alerts left open for over 7 days

name: SentinelOne
description: Checks SentinelOne agents are active and up to date, and no threat is left unresolved.
setup_help: In the SentinelOne console create a service user with the Viewer role (Settings > Users > Service users) and generate an API token. Enter your console URL, e.g. https://acme.sentinelone.net.

tests.title: Agents active and reporting within 7 days
No unresolved threats

name: Datadog
description: Checks logs are kept for 180+ days and alert monitors exist and notify someone.
setup_help: In Datadog go to Organization settings > API keys and Application keys. Create an application key with read scopes (monitors_read, logs_read_config). Pick your Datadog site, e.g. ap1.datadoghq.com.

fields.name: site
fields.label: Datadog site
fields.help: datadoghq.com, us3.datadoghq.com, us5.datadoghq.com, datadoghq.eu, ap1.datadoghq.com, ap2.datadoghq.com

tests.title: Log indexes keep logs for the required period
Alert monitors are configured and notify a person or channel

name: Cloudflare
description: Checks every site forces HTTPS, uses TLS 1.2 or higher and validates the origin certificate.
setup_help: Create an API token in Cloudflare (My Profile > API Tokens) with Zone > Zone Settings: Read for all zones.

tests.title: All sites force HTTPS with TLS 1.2+ and strict origin certificates

name: Scalefusion
description: Checks managed laptops and phones are encrypted, compliant and checking in.
setup_help: In the Scalefusion dashboard go to Integrations > API and generate an API key.

tests.title: Managed devices are encrypted
Managed devices meet compliance policies
Devices checked in within 30 days

name: Hexnode UEM
description: Checks managed laptops and phones are encrypted, compliant and checking in.
setup_help: In Hexnode go to Admin > API, enable API access and copy the key. Enter your portal, e.g. acme.hexnodemdm.com.

tests.title: Managed devices are encrypted
Managed devices meet compliance policies
Devices checked in within 30 days

name: greytHR
description: Imports employees, joining and exit dates for leaver checks and access reviews.
setup_help: Ask greytHR support to enable API access, then create API credentials (client ID and secret) in greytHR Admin > Settings > API. Enter your greytHR domain, e.g. acme.greythr.com.

name: Zoho People
description: Imports employees, managers, joining and exit dates for leaver checks and access reviews.
setup_help: In the Zoho API Console (api-console.zoho.in) create a Self Client, generate a code with scope ZOHOPEOPLE.forms.READ, and exchange it for a refresh token. Pick your Zoho data centre.

name: Freshservice
description: Checks the IT asset inventory is maintained and production changes go through change records.
setup_help: In Freshservice open Profile settings and copy your API key. Enter your domain, e.g. acme.freshservice.com.

tests.title: IT asset inventory maintained and updated in the last 90 days
Changes are recorded through change management
